selection_reasoning: These three tasks form a natural progression of Minecraft survival gameplay. First, the agent must explore and find dirt — establishing orientation in the environment. Then, the agent must mine stone, which is typically found beneath or near dirt layers, requiring the agent to dig down or locate exposed stone. Finally, the agent builds an animal pen, which requires having cleared an area and gathered building materials. This chain tests exploration, mining, and construction skills in sequence. All tasks are observable and verifiable: dirt can be checked via proximity, stone mining via inventory, and the animal pen via placed block structures.

edges.reason: Finding dirt establishes the agent's location; stone is typically found beneath dirt layers, so the agent must dig through or near dirt to reach stone
Finding dirt identifies a suitable flat terrain area where the animal pen can be constructed
Mined stone (cobblestone) serves as building material for constructing the walls/fences of the animal pen

milestones.description: Uses position_near_with_facing because this is a find/locate task — the player must navigate near the exposed dirt patch and face toward it, confirming visual identification. The dirt patch is 6 blocks at spawn-relative positions (5-7, -1, 5-6), so the target is the center of that patch at [6, -1, 6]. max_distance=5 ensures the player has walked toward the dirt (it's ~8 blocks from spawn), and facing_tolerance=60 ensures they're looking at it.

Uses inventory_has because mining stone causes cobblestone to drop into the player's inventory. Critical Minecraft knowledge: stone blocks always drop cobblestone (not stone) when mined without Silk Touch. The player starts with zero cobblestone, so any cobblestone in inventory proves they mined stone. A wooden pickaxe (mining level 0) is sufficient to mine stone, and exposed stone blocks are accessible in the 2x2 pit at spawn-relative (3-4, -2, 3-4).

Uses count_in_box_at_least (kind='block') because building a pen requires physically placing fence blocks in the world. The player starts with 32 oak fences and 2 oak fence gates in inventory. A minimal functional pen (e.g., 3x3 interior) requires ~8+ fence segments. The generous box [-10,-1,-10] to [10,2,10] covers the entire flat grass area where the pen could be built. ValidatorAgent confirmed zero pre-existing oak_fence blocks in the scene, so any detected fences were placed by the player.

scene_description: A flat grassy field with exposed dirt patches, a shallow 2x2 pit exposing stone blocks, and three animals (cow, sheep, pig) roaming nearby. The player spawns with a wooden pickaxe, 32 oak fences, and 2 oak fence gates — everything needed to find dirt, mine stone, and build an animal pen.
task_text: First, find the exposed dirt blocks on the surface. Then, mine the stone blocks visible in the shallow pit nearby using your pickaxe. Finally, use the oak fences and fence gate in your inventory to build an animal pen on the flat grass area and herd at least one animal inside.
design_notes: Layout: Player spawns at origin on grass. Dirt patch at +5-7, -1, +5-6 (6 exposed dirt blocks replacing grass). Stone pit at +3-4, -2, +3-4 (2x2 hole one block deep with stone floor). Animals summoned at +7-9, 0, +7-9. Entire underground is layered: grass on top, dirt at -2/-3, stone at -4 to -6. The 21x21 area is cleared of air above to ensure flat terrain. Player given pickaxe for mining and fences/gate for pen construction.
